cards.anchor: Exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, the other five unchecked, no incorrect-key write, unchanged source scores, latest snapshot loaded before submission, within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Three inspections, three commits and one refresh cost seven simulated minutes. Record every written key and the final snapshot/status map; no production resource is required.
cards.construction: Keep S0 loaded and retain the stipulated row-bound editor. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; inspect/select K5 during 2-3 and commit during 3-4; inspect/select K7 during 4-5 and commit during 5-6. Refresh during 6-7 to load S2. Local statuses persist by key. Check final identities by keys, including the equal-score pair.
cards.defeat: Any incorrect-key write, missing or extra checked key, source-score modification, final snapshot other than S2, or elapsed time exceeding ten minutes defeats the candidate. Successful replay would refute intermediate-refresh necessity only in this model.
cards.mutation: Move the freshness obligation to the completion boundary and omit every intermediate refresh, removing opportunities for loaded order to change between selection and commit.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospective prediction: retained S0 rows 2, 5 and 7 write K2, K5 and K7 respectively; final refresh preserves those statuses by key and loads S2 at minute seven. No mismatch or mismatch-triggered request is predicted.
cards.prediction_rival: A strict per-commit-refresh necessity account predicts failure of the unchanged valued outcome when its prerequisite is omitted, even with final freshness. The supplied trace alone does not establish that necessity.
cards.probe: Replay the stated seven-minute schedule from all-unchecked S0 and log times, loaded snapshots, selected rows, intended keys, actual writes, mismatch requests and final statuses. Compare the observed result against the strict necessity prediction. The stipulated select-refresh-commit miswrite supplies a diagnostic reference, not an observed successful completion or repeating loop.
cards.rival: Reliable fixed-key correction requires a refresh immediately before each commit; stale loaded scores prevent correct completion.
unknowns: This completion replay has not been executed.
Actual editor binding and human interruption costs are unknown.
Concurrency, key deletion and load failures are excluded; success would support only the eight-record model.
Absence of mismatch in this replay would not establish or disprove feedback recurrence elsewhere.

cards.anchor: Preserve the same exact three corrections, zero incorrect-key writes, read-only scores, latest-snapshot compliance and ten-minute ceiling while allowing refresh between selection and commit.
cards.burden: Use the supplied immutable-key control and nine one-minute actions. A single extra request-gate slot raises each matched completion arm to ten minutes. Diagnostic controls are separate replays and may fail the outcome.
cards.construction: Bind each selected edit to its inspected immutable key. For K2, K5 and K7 sequentially perform inspect/select, refresh, commit during 0-3, 3-6 and 6-9. Refreshes finish at minutes 2, 5 and 8; the final loaded source is S2. Commit through the retained key binding rather than the current row occupant. Verify equal-score targets by keys.
cards.defeat: A wrong-key write with retained immutable-key binding, incorrect final statuses, changed source scores, stale final snapshot or over-budget completion defeats the candidate. A frozen-row miswrite would also contradict reordering as the sufficient cause. An extra request without a later wrong write is not evidence of recurrence.
cards.mutation: Separate edit identity from display position and separate mismatch notifications from logged write correctness, exposing the two proposed causal arrows independently.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospective prediction: key-bound completion writes K2, K5 and K7 only and finishes at minute nine. In the initial 0-3 diagnostic, only changing-snapshot row binding writes K5 when K2 is intended; frozen-row and both key-bound controls write K2. Injected mismatch notification may request refresh despite a correct write, but preserved key identity predicts no resulting wrong-key write.
cards.prediction_rival: A snapshot-change account independent of selection binding predicts the changing key-bound control also fails. A notification-driven error account predicts later wrong writes after injected notifications despite preserved key identity. These are rival hypotheses, not supplied observations.
cards.probe: First cross frozen/changing snapshots with row/key binding under the identical stipulated 0-3 actions. Then replay the nine-minute key-bound completion, adding one matched slot after the first commit: inject a mismatch notification and perform its requested refresh, or withhold it and spend the slot inspecting. Keep ordinary actions matched and final S2 compliance; log refresh requests separately from actual writes. A single return request cannot establish a repeating loop.
cards.rival: Changing source snapshots or mismatch notifications cause correction errors independently of whether an edit retains immutable target identity.
unknowns: All proposed control and completion outcomes remain unexecuted hypotheses.
Synthetic key binding does not establish binding in real editors.
Detection rates, usability costs and excluded concurrency/load failures limit transfer; unavailable production resources are unnecessary for these model probes.
